proposals.evidence: Buddruss Grangali kandā́ wild almond matches Turner kāntā 3030: Kalasha kānda almond and Khowar kándu wild almond tree are explicit neighboring comparanda. The source contrasts this wild almond with edible Persian bādām.

proposals.evidence: Buddruss lists -lām as a village suffix in Grangali place names Cukon-lām and Wuriglām. Turner grāma 4368 explicitly lists Ningalami and Shumashti lām village, as well as Pashai lām, in the same regional stem. This link records the inherited village element in a bound name component; it does not reclassify the source suffix as a free noun.
